root_cause: rich 14.3.2 rewrote split_graphemes as a while-loop in which two branches never advance `index`: (1) a zero-width non-special character (e.g. ANSI ESC \x1b, which get_character_cell_size now returns 0 for) when `spans` is still empty, because the branch is `elif spans:`; (2) a VS16 (\ufe0f) when `last_measured_character` is None, because the branch is `elif last_measured_character:`. So Console.print('\x1b[...') or any string that starts with a zero-width char or a lone VS16 hangs forever. A third edge: a trailing ZWJ does `index += 2` and pushes the span end past len(text).
best_solution: Make every branch of the loop consume at least one codepoint and keep the invariant that spans cover every string index with no gaps (callers such as chop_cells/_split_text slice text by span starts/ends). In split_graphemes: (a) if the char is ZWJ or VS16 and there are no spans yet, append a zero-width span (index, index+1, 0) and continue; (b) ZWJ: keep `index += 2` (it swallows the joined next codepoint into the previous grapheme, which the existing family-emoji tests depend on) but clamp to +1 when the ZWJ is the last char; extend spans[-1]; (c) VS16: always `index += 1`; if last_measured_character is set apply the narrow-to-wide +1 width, otherwise just extend spans[-1]; (d) zero-width non-special char: extend spans[-1] if any, else append (index, index+1, 0). Result: '\x1b' -> ([(0,1,0)], 0), '\x1b\x1b' -> ([(0,2,0)], 0), '\u200d\u200d' -> ([(0,2,0)], 0), and chop_cells('\x1b', 3) -> [] because line_size stays 0.
acceptable_alternatives: Any restructuring that guarantees progress on every iteration, keeps ZWJ consuming the following codepoint (index += 2, clamped at end), and emits a leading zero-width span (start, end, 0) that later zero-width chars merge into, rather than silently skipping leading zero-width chars. A plain `index += 1` fallback that drops those chars from the span list fixes the hang but fails the 6 new split_graphemes cases.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py: new test_chop_cells_zero_width parametrized over '', '\x1b', '\x1b\x1b', '\x1b\x1b\x1b', '\x1b\x1b\x1b\x1b' all expecting chop_cells(text, 3) == []. test_split_graphemes gains exact span expectations: '\x1b' -> [(0,1,0)],0; '\x1b\x1b' -> [(0,2,0)],0; '\ufe0f' -> [(0,1,0)],0; '\ufe0f\ufe0f' -> [(0,2,0)],0; '\u200d' -> [(0,1,0)],0; '\u200d\u200d' -> [(0,2,0)],0, and cell_len(text) must agree. Pre-existing test_split_text / test_split_graphemes cases for FM = '\U0001f469\u200d\U0001f527' (width 2, one span (0,3,2)) must keep passing, so the ZWJ += 2 step must not change.
locating_signals: Statement names the function split_graphemes (rich/cells.py) and the symptom 'infinite loop'; the linked issue (not visible to the agent) says the trigger is ANSI escape \x1b returning width 0. Reading the while-loop shows two branches guarded by `elif spans:` / `elif last_measured_character:` with no else, i.e. no index advance.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed. v4 (79 calls) only changed the ZWJ step from += 2 to += 1: breaks ZWJ emoji joining (5 existing test_split_text FM cases fail) and leaves the \x1b hang, so the run times out after 40 tests. v6 also changed ZWJ to += 1 and added `else: index += 1` for zero-width chars with no spans, fixing the \x1b hang but dropping the char (spans [] instead of [(0,1,0)]); it left the VS16-without-previous-char branch non-advancing, so it hangs on '\ufe0f' after 60 tests. v7 only added `else: index += 1` to the VS16 branch; the \x1b leading-zero-width hang remains and the run times out at test 41. v8 fixed all hangs (ZWJ += 1, VS16 always advances, zero-width else index += 1) but produced 14 failures: 8 pre-existing ZWJ/FM cases (family emoji now splits into two width-2 graphemes) and 6 new cases because leading zero-width chars were skipped instead of recorded as (i, i+1, 0) spans; it also left repro.py and reproduce_issue.py in the repo. Common error: the agent mistook the intentional ZWJ `index += 2` for the bug and never ran the existing tests/test_cells.py, which would have caught it.
generalizable_lesson: For an 'infinite loop' fix, find each loop branch that can finish without advancing the cursor (an `elif cond:` with no else) and add the missing advance there. Leave the step sizes of branches that already make progress alone: an unusual step like `+= 2` is usually intentional (here it consumes the joined codepoint). Keep the output's structural invariant, here that spans cover every index, by emitting an empty or zero-weight element instead of silently skipping input. Then run the module's existing test file before finishing. Existing tests would have caught 3 of our 4 regressions.
